div.l: But he laft nat / for reyn ne for thondir Prologꝰus
In siknesse ne in myscheff to visite
The ferthest in his paryssh mochill and lyte
Vpon his feet and in his honde / a staff
This noble ensample / to his sheep he yaff
And ferst he wrowht / and aftirward he tawhte
Out of the gospell / he tho wordys cawhte
And this figure / he added eek therto
Yf gold rost / what shall Iren do
For if a prest be foul / on whom we trust
No wondir is / a lewde man to rust
And shame it is / if a prest take kepe
Off a shetene sheperde / and a clene shepe
Wel awht a prest / ensample for to yeven
Bi his clennesse / howe his sheep shuld lyven
He set nat his benefis / to hire
And let his sheep / accombre in the myre
And ran vnto londoıı̄un / vnto seynt poulis
To seken him a chawntrye for sowlys
Or wᵗith a brethirhed / to ben wytholde
But dwellyd at hom / and kep wel his foulde
So that the wolf / maade it nat myskarye
He was a sheperde / and nat a mecennarye
And thauh. he / hooly werk and v̉ertuous
He was nat to synful men / dispitous
Ne of his speche Daungerous / ne digne
But in his speche / discrete and benigne
To drawen folk to heuene / bi fairenesse
Bi good ensample / this was his besynesse
But it were any ꝑpersone / obstynat
What so he were / of hie or lowe estat
Hym wolde he snybbyn / sharply for the noones
A bettir prest / I trowe nowher noon is
